messages:
sara: Orbit Labs reported a production parser failure after last night's split-region rollout. They say our /v1/generate returned the metadata field as an escaped JSON string instead of an object. request_id=req_0ab3f9c2, customer pipeline throws JSONDecodeError when ingesting.

sara: quick example they sent (redacted):
```
POST /v1/generate
Body: {
  \"prompt\": \"extract event\",
  \"output_format\": \"strict_json\"
}

Response 200:
{
  \"id\": \"resp_abc\",
  \"result\": {
    \"event\": \"purchase\",
    \"metadata\": \"{\\\"user_id\\\":123,\\\"items\\\":[\\\"sku-1\\\"]}\"  <-- STRING, should be object
  }
}
```

nate: can you paste the full raw response headers and the exact model/route they hit? also the request_id you pasted (req_0ab3f9c2) — I'll search logs.

sara: headers: \"x-request-id: req_0ab3f9c2\", x-route: \"/generate:rw-instruct-1-large\". Model: rw-instruct-1-large, route config has output_mode=strict_json. Customer says this started after the region-split rollout yesterday ~2026-03-15 22:09Z.

deploy-bot: Deployed: service=serve-v3.1 regions=us-east-1,eu-west-1 at 2026-03-15T22:10:13Z by build/deploy-2026.3.15-22

nate: found the request in logs. The request did hit a fallback kernel for short sequences: kernel_variant=lite-kernel-quant. There was a string_serializer path used when record size < 512 tokens. Possible regression where nested JSON objects get run through escape-string branch. Reproducing locally now with the same model and route config.

sara: customer repro curl they ran (they sanitized keys):
```bash
curl -X POST https://api.redwood.ai/v1/generate \
  -H 'Authorization: Bearer <key>' \
  -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
  -d '{"prompt":"extract event","output_format":"strict_json"}'
```
They get 200 but their ingest parser fails with: JSONDecodeError: Expecting value: line 1 column 2 (char 1). Our response has metadata as a quoted string.

jon: severity? is this blocking for multiple customers or just Orbit?

sara: blocking for Orbit (multi-tenant pipeline). They can't write events to S3 because downstream JSON schema validation rejects the stringified metadata. They turned on permissive parsing as a temporary workaround but want a fix asap.

frank: quick mitigation option: add a transform on the route to run JSON.parse on metadata if it's a string before sending to the customer (server-side fix) — can do as a config-level patch to route transformers while eng ships a proper fix.

nate: agree. root cause looks like: when we fall back to lite-kernel we accidentally serialize nested objects via escape_string_serializer. I'll open a hotfix PR to disable the escape path for strict_json routes and pin the route to kernel=stable-3.0 as immediate rollback. PR: github.com/redwood/serve/pull/2745 (draft). Will coordinate rollback for affected routes.

nate: action items: 1) frank to patch route transformer (short-term) 2) nate to land PR and prepare canary rollback for routes using strict_json 3) sara to notify Orbit and provide workaround script. ETA: hotfix in next 2 hours, rollback if needed in 4 hours.

sara: thanks. I'll loop in Orbit and escalate to their engineering lead. Please include the sample request/response in the customer note and the request_id req_0ab3f9c2.

frank: I'll push the transformer change to the customer route config now and verify with a smoke test.

nate: smoke test passed against pinned kernel. Leaving this thread open until full rollout of hotfix and customer confirmation.

sara: noted — will update when Orbit confirms ingestion is green. :white_check_mark:
